scope: Three-protocol Wi-Fi/MQTT application fixed memory; unchanged group/total caps; runtime heap/stack and hardware acceptance unqualified

evidence_basis.policy: Image-specific module reservations use the linked transaction map. MQTT target payload 112/packet 384. Task-pool cap and existing group/total limits unchanged. Compact configuration views share their 4096-byte workspace with up to four temporary TLS intermediate records. Parser state reserves 25 bytes and the shared store with its ownership state reserves 4105 bytes; the unused cJSON mutable-state reservation is retired. Four enabled driver workspaces use 35496 linked bytes in c3app with shared USB request/reply storage while retaining eight profile entries. Fixed ESP-TLS contexts, error records and hostname scratch reserve 3168 bytes from reclaimed application capacity. Fixed TLS buffers, hostname, outer state, temporary certificate head and peer digest reserve 25532 bytes for the single MQTT session, including the full 16717-byte input capacity in a 16720-byte aligned slot, a separate 254-byte hostname slot, and two typed transforms, two sessions and one handshake record (2872 typed bytes with tickets disabled), one 952-byte temporary peer-chain head and one 32-byte peer digest, a 64-byte PRF seed, 22-byte label and two 66-byte stores for the imported key and key-derived secret, plus scope/lease metadata. Fixed lwIP socket, TCP connection, listener and segment records and eight input plus eight callback messages, two UDP endpoints and seven pending ARP entries and twelve TCP/IP timer records reserve 1789 bytes, including slot occupancy. No group or aggregate cap increases. Queue ring metadata is reserved only for the eight queue slots. The station reserves five TCP transport packets and two IP control packets, including header storage and the split flag. Eight receive references reserve 224 bytes. The station reserves 17 bytes for one IGMP group and its occupancy flag. The transaction adapter reserves 813 bytes. DHCP reserves one station state and two outgoing messages independently of TCP. The ARP request/reply frame, a UDP header and one untagged Ethernet frame for ARP copying or Wi-Fi transmission are independent of TCP packets. The default station reserves the native registry node, typed interface and IP records, two identifying strings and a separate hostname lease. Only semaphore slots reserve counts and only mutex slots reserve ownership and recursion depth. Queue keys identify live slots and only queues reserve a second native handle. Current module ceilings for the station, transaction and configuration path use the linked sizes for this image so their sum stays within the application limit.
